decision.engineering_decision: Choose the gap and coupling length of a symmetric silicon directional coupler for a cross-power ratio over a 100 nm band, with its complex response for phase-sensitive circuits.
decision.intended_use: Predict the cross power and the unwrapped common phase at five wavelengths of the declared local-supermode reference (10 nm supermode tables) over the DEVELOPMENT population; agreement is with that model, not with 3D FDTD or a fabricated device. A phase-aware test Challenge: for this symmetric family the reference is itself the conventional design method, so it exercises the pipeline on complex outputs rather than demonstrating engineering value (ticket D2).

design_variables.description: Straight coupling length, 1 to 6; cosine S-bends of 3.0 and 2.0 um to a 1.6 um port pitch are fixed.
design_variables.name: length_um

limits.basis: Reference numerical check: four times the z points may move the cross power by at most this (pilot worst 7e-9).
limits.name: check_z_integration_cross

limits.basis: Reference numerical check on the common phase (pilot worst 3.5e-8 rad).
limits.name: check_z_integration_phase

limits.basis: Table check: every supermode's mirror parity within this of +-1 (built tables: within 1e-6).
limits.name: table_parity

limits.basis: Table check: every supermode's relative eigen-residual at most this (built tables: about 4e-14).
limits.name: table_residual

limits.basis: Provisional DEVELOPMENT value: the strongest couplers (cross power at 1.55 um of 0.10 or more); the signed cross-power bias is reported there, not scored.
limits.name: important_region_cross

next_experiment: Integrate the miner path (CHALLENGE-PHOTONIC-02), then decide whether to build the v2 asymmetric coupler (eigenmode expansion, no paid compute) or fund the costed 3D comparison.

outputs.description: The unwrapped common phase (phi_even + phi_odd)/2 at the five wavelengths (predicted).
outputs.name: common_phase_rad

outputs.description: Complex S31 and S41 per wavelength: derived by Carbon from the two outputs under the port convention (arg(S41/S31) = -pi/2 exactly), never predicted.
outputs.name: s_parameters

pilots.note: 8 ordinary public draws and 4 box corners, each with four refinement pairs (z integration, ladder, 20 and 5 nm meshes) against the committed 10 nm tables. The v3 record's 3D FDTD diagnostics belong to the superseded reference and stay with v3.

population.proposed: carbon.photonic-coupler.development-population.v1: independent uniform draws over the gap and length box (Q = P, w = 1). A proposed DEVELOPMENT population, not a ratified production one.

recommendation.basis: All 12 pilot cases ran OK; the 10 nm reference's remaining mesh error (about 0.3 % in the phase difference, 0.03 rad in the common phase) is about a fiftieth of the closed-form baseline's error (score 1.1 to 1.7); the phase convention is exact by construction; the pools and both baselines are scored through the exam (private pool: closed-form 1.446, learned 5.8e-4).

reference.applicability: The declared box (gap 150 to 300 nm, length 1 to 6 um, 1.50 to 1.60 um). Mesh error about 0.3 % in the phase difference and 0.03 rad in the common phase; a grid-alignment wobble of at most about 7e-3 rad and 0.5 % in cross power is part of the declared tables. Agreement with 3D FDTD is supported at the 5 to 10 % level only.
reference.licence: Carbon's own code; numpy and scipy are BSD-3-Clause
reference.model: Local-supermode model of a symmetric 500 x 220 nm silicon coupler in silica (n 3.48, 1.444): even and odd supermode indices tabulated on a 41-gap ladder at 10 nm and integrated along the gap profile; radiation, reflection and bend loss are outside it
reference.solver: Carbon's full-vector FDFD mode solver (carbon/photonic/modes.py) with sub-pixel permittivity averaging; numpy 2.4.6 and scipy 1.17.1 (ARPACK with a fixed start vector)

unresolved: The reference is the local-supermode model, not 3D FDTD; a radiation-inclusive comparison at 10 nm or finer is paid compute (about 14 GPU-hours, costed in the ticket) and needs its own owner grant.

For the symmetric family the reference is the conventional design method, so a learned model can only reproduce it (ticket D2); the value version is the v2 asymmetric coupler or fabrication variation.
The tables are not smoothed; their grid-alignment wobble sets the exam's resolution floor near 1e-3.
Miner-path integration is CHALLENGE-PHOTONIC-02; the registry entry stays RESERVED until then.
Every value above is a provisional DEVELOPMENT value; scientific, security and launch review are human-reserved.
